steps: Paste a JSON object or array into the input panel.
Choose Beautify for indentation or Minify to remove whitespace.
Check the validation status, then copy the formatted output.
faq: What happens when the JSON is invalid?
The formatter leaves the output unchanged and shows the browser parse error.
Does formatting change values or key order?
No. It only changes whitespace; parsed object keys keep their original order.

steps: Paste HTML markup into the input panel.
Select Beautify to indent nested elements or Minify to compact the markup.
Copy the cleaned markup from the output panel.
faq: Does this render my HTML?
No. It formats the markup as text and does not execute scripts.
Can I minify a full document?
Yes. Paste a complete HTML document or a fragment.

steps: Paste CSS rules into the input panel.
Select Beautify for readable declarations or Minify for a compact stylesheet.
Copy the result for your stylesheet or build process.
faq: Will formatting change CSS behavior?
No. The tool changes whitespace and punctuation layout only.
Can I use CSS variables and media queries?
Yes. They are treated as regular CSS text.

steps: Paste a SQL query into the input panel.
Click Beautify to place clauses and conditions on readable lines.
Review and copy the formatted query.
faq: Does it execute my query?
No. It only formats text in your browser.
Which SQL dialect is required?
The formatter is syntax-light and is useful for common SQL query layouts.

steps: Paste an XML document or fragment.
Choose Beautify to indent elements or Minify to remove spacing between tags.
Copy the resulting XML and inspect the status message.
faq: Does it validate against an XSD?
No. Use the XSD Validator when you also need a schema-root check.
Are attributes preserved?
Yes. Formatting keeps element attributes and text content.

steps: Paste a YAML document into the input panel.
Click Format / Validate to parse and re-emit the document.
Copy the normalized YAML or correct the displayed parse error.
faq: Does it support nested lists and objects?
Yes. YAML structures are parsed and emitted with indentation.
Will comments be retained?
No. YAML comments are not preserved when the document is re-emitted.

steps: Paste the JavaScript you want to compress.
Click Minify JS to remove comments and unnecessary whitespace.
Copy the compact result for a production bundle or snippet.
faq: Does minification rename variables?
No. This lightweight minifier preserves identifiers.
Should I minify third-party code here?
For complex production code, use your project bundler as the final minification step.

steps: Enter plain text or a Base64 value.
Click Encode to create Base64, or Decode to recover the original text.
Copy the converted value from the output panel.
faq: Is Base64 encryption?
No. Base64 is an encoding and can be decoded by anyone.
Does it handle Unicode text?
Yes. Text is encoded through browser-safe UTF-8 handling.

steps: Paste the URL component, query value, or encoded text.
Choose Encode for safe percent encoding or Decode to read encoded characters.
Copy the resulting string into your URL or request.
faq: Should I encode a whole URL?
Usually encode query values or path components, not separators such as : and /.
Why does decoding fail?
Malformed percent sequences cannot be decoded and produce an error.

steps: Paste text or HTML containing special characters.
Click Encode to turn reserved characters into entities, or Decode to restore them.
Copy the converted text for use in markup.
faq: When should I encode entities?
Encode text that will be inserted into HTML so characters like < and & are displayed literally.
Does decoding run embedded HTML?
No. The result remains plain text in the output area.

steps: Enter the exact text or content to fingerprint.
Select SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512.
Click Generate Hash and copy the hexadecimal digest.
faq: Can a hash be reversed?
No. Cryptographic hashes are one-way fingerprints.
Why do tiny changes produce a new hash?
A single character change creates a substantially different digest by design.

steps: Paste a compact JWT with its three dot-separated sections.
Read the decoded header and payload in the output panel.
Inspect claims such as exp, sub, iss, and the declared algorithm.
faq: Does decoding verify the signature?
No. Decoding only reads Base64URL data; it does not establish trust.
Can I decode an expired token?
Yes. Expiration does not prevent the header and payload from being displayed.

steps: Edit the header JSON and payload claims.
Keep alg set to HS256 and enter the HMAC signing secret.
Click Sign JWT, then copy the generated token.
faq: Which signing algorithm is supported?
This tool signs HS256 tokens using the Web Crypto API.
Is my signing secret sent anywhere?
No. Signing runs locally in your browser.

steps: Choose an image file or paste a complete image data URL.
Confirm the decoded preview appears below the input.
Copy the data URL or download the previewed image.
faq: Which image formats work?
Any image format your browser can read can be encoded as a data URL.
Is the image uploaded?
No. Image conversion and previewing happen locally in your browser.

steps: Paste the original text on the left and the revised text on the right.
Adjust whitespace, wrapping, and word-or-character comparison options.
Use the change navigation controls to inspect additions and removals.
faq: What does Ignore whitespace do?
It treats runs of spaces and leading or trailing whitespace as equivalent.
Can I compare source code?
Yes. The tool compares any plain text side by side.

steps: Enter a regular expression pattern and optional flags such as g or i.
Paste the text to test against it.
Review every match and captured result in the output panel.
faq: Which regex flavor is used?
Patterns use the JavaScript regular expression engine in your browser.
Why is my pattern invalid?
The status message reports JavaScript syntax errors such as unclosed groups.

steps: Paste the JSON you need to check.
Edit the input while watching the validation status update.
Use the parse error location to correct invalid syntax.
faq: Does it reformat valid JSON?
This page validates only; use JSON Formatter when you also want indentation.
Are comments allowed in JSON?
No. Standard JSON does not allow comments or trailing commas.

steps: Paste a JSON object or array.
Enter a simple path such as $.project.items[0].name.
Read the matched value or the path error in the result panel.
faq: Which JSONPath expressions are supported?
Use root $, dot properties, bracket properties, numeric indexes, and wildcard selections.
Can I query invalid JSON?
No. Correct the JSON parse error before running a path.

steps: Paste the XML document in the XML panel.
Paste the associated XSD schema in the schema panel.
Review XML syntax and the root-element compatibility status.
faq: Is this a complete XSD validator?
It checks XML syntax and schema root hints; it does not implement full server-side XSD validation.
Can I validate namespaces?
Namespace-aware schema documents can be inspected, but use a full validator for strict conformance.

steps: Paste CSV text, including a header row when available.
Review the parsed rows in the table below the input.
Correct delimiters or quotes in the source if columns are misaligned.
faq: Are quoted commas supported?
Yes. The parser recognizes quoted CSV fields.
Does the first row become headers?
Yes. The first parsed row is displayed as the table header.

steps: Paste the original JSON and the modified JSON.
Review the table of added, removed, and changed paths.
Use each path to identify the affected nested key or array value.
faq: Does key order matter?
No. Parsed object keys are compared by name and value.
Can it compare nested structures?
Yes. Changes are reported with paths through nested objects and arrays.

steps: Paste .env lines in KEY=value form.
Review the formatted output and any duplicate or malformed-entry errors.
Copy the cleaned file contents back to your environment file.
faq: Are duplicate keys flagged?
Yes. The tool reports repeated environment variable names.
Are secrets uploaded?
No. The .env text is processed locally in your browser.

steps: Paste JSON or XML into the input area.
Click JSON to XML or XML to JSON to select the conversion direction.
Review the output and copy the converted document.
faq: What root element is used for JSON to XML?
JSON output is wrapped in a root element so it forms a valid XML document.
Can XML attributes be round-tripped exactly?
The converter focuses on element data; complex XML features may not round-trip exactly.

steps: Paste a JSON array of objects or a CSV table.
Select JSON to CSV or CSV to JSON.
Copy the converted records from the output panel.
faq: What JSON shape converts best to CSV?
Use an array of flat objects, with one object for each CSV row.
How are missing fields handled?
CSV cells are left blank when a record does not provide a header field.

steps: Paste CSV rows or XML records into the input field.
Choose CSV to XML or XML to CSV.
Review and copy the generated record representation.
faq: What XML structure is produced?
CSV rows become record-style XML elements below a records root.
Can XML with nested elements become CSV?
Flat, repeated record elements work best; nested data may need normalization first.

steps: Paste a variable name, phrase, or block of text.
Choose camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, PascalCase, or CONSTANT_CASE.
Copy the converted name from the output panel.
faq: Does it handle acronyms such as APIResponse?
Yes. Acronym runs are split into readable words before conversion.
Can I convert multiple lines?
Yes. Each line is converted independently.

steps: Paste YAML or JSON into the input area.
Choose YAML to JSON or JSON to YAML.
Fix any parsing error, then copy the converted document.
faq: Does YAML support comments?
Input comments can be parsed, but they are not preserved in generated output.
Can I convert arrays and nested objects?
Yes. Both directions support standard nested data structures.

steps: Enter an integer in the Number field.
Select the base that describes the input value.
Read the binary, octal, decimal, and hexadecimal equivalents.
faq: Can I enter hexadecimal letters?
Yes. Select Hexadecimal and use digits 0-9 and letters A-F.
Does it support fractions?
No. This converter is for whole integers.

steps: Write or paste Markdown in the left panel.
Watch the raw HTML update as you edit.
Copy the HTML into your template or content system.
faq: Does it render a visual preview?
This page provides raw HTML; use Markdown Preview for a rendered view.
Which Markdown features work?
Headings, emphasis, lists, links, code, and common block elements are supported.

steps: Paste HTML markup in the input panel.
Review the Markdown generated beside it.
Copy the Markdown and adjust any semantic details as needed.
faq: Will all HTML round-trip perfectly?
No. Complex layouts and custom attributes do not always have Markdown equivalents.
Are headings and lists converted?
Yes. Common semantic tags are converted to their Markdown forms.

steps: Paste a cURL command with its URL, headers, and body.
Choose Fetch, Axios, or Python as the target client.
Copy the generated request code and replace example credentials if needed.
faq: Are request headers preserved?
Yes. Parsed -H headers are included in the generated request.
Does it execute the command?
No. It converts the command without sending a network request.

steps: Choose an image from your device.
Set the output width, height, and JPEG quality.
Click Resize and download the generated JPEG preview.
faq: Does resizing keep the aspect ratio automatically?
Width and height are explicit, so set both proportionally when you need to preserve it.
Is my image uploaded?
No. Resizing occurs in a browser canvas on your device.

steps: Choose a square source image for best results.
Click Download favicon ZIP to create the icon bundle.
Extract the ZIP to get an ICO file and common PNG favicon sizes.
faq: Which sizes are included?
The ZIP includes 16, 32, 180, 192, and 512 pixel PNG icons plus favicon.ico.
Is the source image uploaded?
No. All favicon files are generated locally.

steps: Paste an X12 or EDIFACT interchange into the input panel.
Review the detected format and formatted segment output.
Use the validation messages to correct missing envelopes or separators.
faq: Which EDI formats are recognized?
The tool recognizes common X12 and EDIFACT segment separators.
Does it validate transaction-set business rules?
It formats segments and reports basic structural issues, not full trading-partner validation.

steps: Paste an X12 or EDIFACT message.
Review the table of segment tags, element positions, annotations, and values.
Use the rows to trace a field back to its source segment.
faq: Can I inspect a full interchange?
Yes. Paste the complete message and every parsed segment is listed.
Are segment names shown?
Known segment tags are annotated with readable names where available.

steps: Paste an X12 or EDIFACT message.
Review the detected format, validation errors, and segment hierarchy JSON.
Copy the JSON for inspection or downstream processing.
faq: Does the JSON retain element positions?
Yes. Each element includes its position, name when known, and value.
Is this a standards-complete EDI mapping?
It creates an inspectable segment representation rather than a trading-partner-specific map.

steps: Choose how many UUIDs to create, from 1 to 100.
Click Generate UUIDs.
Copy one or more UUID v4 values from the output.
faq: What UUID version is generated?
The tool uses crypto.randomUUID to generate version 4 UUIDs.
Are UUIDs random enough for identifiers?
They use your browser's cryptographic random generator.

steps: Enter the URL, text, or other content to encode.
Wait for the QR preview to update automatically.
Download the generated code as a PNG image.
faq: Can a QR code contain plain text?
Yes. URLs, text, contact details, and other text payloads can be encoded.
Does it track scans?
No. The generator creates an image only and does not track its use.

steps: Set a password length from 8 to 128 characters.
Choose the character groups to include.
Click Generate and copy a password from the output.
faq: Are generated passwords stored?
No. They are generated locally and are not saved by Codepackr.
Why include several character groups?
A larger character set generally increases password entropy.

steps: Choose paragraphs, sentences, or words.
Enter how many units you need.
Copy the generated placeholder text.
faq: Can I generate a single sentence?
Yes. Select Sentences and set the count to one.
Is this content suitable for production?
No. Lorem ipsum is intended as design and layout placeholder copy.

steps: Paste the text you want to analyze or transform.
Choose a transformation such as title case, sorting, deduplication, cleanup, or replace.
Review the live counts and copy the resulting text.
faq: What does Remove Duplicates do?
It removes repeated lines while preserving the first occurrence.
Can I replace text?
Yes. Enter Find and Replace values, then click Replace.

steps: Write or paste Markdown in the editor.
Review the rendered preview beside the source.
Iterate on headings, lists, links, and emphasis until the preview is correct.
faq: Does the preview execute scripts?
No. Markdown is rendered as content rather than executable page code.
Can I preview lists and code blocks?
Yes. Common Markdown block formatting is displayed in the preview.

steps: Choose a color with the picker or enter a HEX value.
Review the converted RGB and HSL values.
Copy the format required by your stylesheet or design token.
faq: Can I enter shorthand HEX?
Use a full six-digit HEX value for the most reliable conversion.
Does it support alpha values?
The current converter focuses on opaque HEX, RGB, and HSL colors.

steps: Enter a Unix timestamp or select a local date and time.
Read the matching ISO date and Unix seconds value.
Copy the format required by your API, log, or database.
faq: Are Unix timestamps in seconds or milliseconds?
This tool accepts and produces Unix timestamps in seconds.
Which time zone is shown?
The date input is local time; the converted ISO value is displayed in UTC.

steps: Enter a five-field cron expression such as 0 9 * * 1-5.
Read the plain-English schedule explanation.
Review the next five local run times and correct any invalid field.
faq: Which cron format is supported?
Use the standard five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week.
What time zone are upcoming runs in?
Next run times are shown in your browser's local time zone.

steps: Paste the title or phrase you want in a URL.
Review the lowercase, hyphen-separated slug generated beside it.
Copy the slug for a route, filename, or permalink.
faq: How are spaces handled?
Runs of spaces become a single hyphen.
What happens to punctuation?
Unsupported punctuation is removed to keep the slug URL-safe.

steps: Search by numeric code, status name, or a word such as redirect.
Review the matching HTTP status rows.
Use the description to choose or diagnose the correct response code.
faq: Can I search a partial code?
Yes. The filter matches code numbers and status text.
Does it include every HTTP status?
It includes commonly used informational, success, redirect, client-error, and server-error codes.

steps: Define one field per line as name:type.
Choose the number of records to generate.
Copy the JSON array, using supported types such as uuid, email, date, and boolean.
faq: Which field types are supported?
Use string, number, boolean, date, uuid, or email.
Can I generate more than one record?
Yes. Set Records from 1 to 100.

steps: Type an arithmetic expression or use the calculator keypad.
Use operators, parentheses, powers, and sqrt where needed.
Read the computed result and adjust the expression if the status reports an error.
faq: What operations are supported?
The calculator supports addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, powers, parentheses, and square roots.
Does it evaluate arbitrary JavaScript?
No. Only supported math expressions are accepted.

steps: Enter the amount you plan to invest each month.
Set your expected annual return rate and investment period.
Review the invested amount, estimated returns, and projected maturity value.
faq: What is a SIP?
A systematic investment plan is a regular, usually monthly investment into a fund or other investment.
Are SIP returns guaranteed?
No. The calculated return is an estimate based on the rate you enter; actual market returns can vary.

steps: Enter the total loan amount you intend to borrow.
Set the annual interest rate and repayment term in years.
Review the estimated monthly EMI, total interest, and total repayment amount.
faq: What is EMI?
EMI means equated monthly installment: the fixed monthly amount used to repay a loan over its term.
Does this include fees or insurance?
No. This estimate uses only the loan amount, interest rate, and term. Add lender fees or insurance separately.

steps: Paste or type the text you want to measure.
Review the live word, character, sentence, and line counts.
Use the counts to check a draft against a length or readability limit.
faq: Are spaces included in the character count?
The character count reflects the text as entered, including spaces and punctuation.
How are words separated?
Words are identified from runs of non-whitespace text, so punctuation remains attached to its neighboring word.

steps: Paste the text whose length you need to check.
Read the character count update as you edit, including spaces and punctuation.
Copy or revise the text until it fits your target limit.
faq: Does the count include spaces?
Yes. Spaces and punctuation are part of the entered text and are included.
Can I use it for social media limits?
Yes. It provides a quick local count for captions, titles, messages, and form fields.

steps: Paste the multiline text into the editor.
Review the number of lines, including the effect of blank lines.
Adjust the text and use the updated count for file or content limits.
faq: Is a blank line counted?
Yes. A line break creates a line position, including blank lines in the input.
Does it upload my text?
No. The count is calculated locally in your browser.

steps: Paste the paragraph or document into the editor.
Review the detected sentence count as the text changes.
Use the result to check document structure or reading-length targets.
faq: How are sentences detected?
Sentence endings are inferred from common terminal punctuation such as periods, question marks, and exclamation marks.
Are abbreviations always handled perfectly?
No. Punctuation-based detection can interpret some abbreviations as sentence endings.

steps: Paste the lines you want to clean.
Run the duplicate-line action to keep the first occurrence of each repeated line.
Review and copy the deduplicated output.
faq: Which duplicate is kept?
The first occurrence is preserved and later identical lines are removed.
Does line order change?
No. The remaining lines keep their original order.

steps: Paste text containing blank or whitespace-only lines.
Run the cleanup action to remove empty lines.
Copy the compacted text from the output.
faq: Are whitespace-only lines removed?
Yes. Lines with no visible content are treated as empty.
Are non-empty lines changed?
No. Content on non-empty lines is preserved.

steps: Paste text containing repeated spaces or tabs.
Run the cleanup action to collapse excess horizontal whitespace.
Review and copy the normalized text.
faq: Are line breaks preserved?
Yes. The cleanup targets repeated spaces and tabs without merging separate lines.
Can it clean copied spreadsheet text?
Yes. It is useful for normalizing text copied from tables or formatted documents.

steps: Paste one item per line into the editor.
Run the alphabetical sort action.
Review the ordered lines and copy the result for your list or file.
faq: Are duplicate lines removed while sorting?
No. Sorting changes order only; duplicate entries remain.
Is sorting case-sensitive?
The result follows the tool's text comparison behavior, so review mixed-case lists when exact ordering matters.

steps: Paste the multiline content into the editor.
Run the reverse action to invert the line sequence.
Review the output and copy the reversed block.
faq: Are lines changed internally?
No. Each line's text is preserved while the line order is reversed.
What happens to blank lines?
Blank lines remain in the sequence and move with their positions.
